input.quote: 10. NONASSIGNABILITY. Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: Section 10 subjects every assignment, including an assignment by Clear Capital to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, to RadialSpark's prior written consent. There is no M&A or affiliate carve-out anywhere in the Agreement (the preamble contains no successors/assigns language), so the clause fails the fallback elements requiring that both parties may assign to a successor on written notice. The consent standard itself is already mutual and qualified as "not... unreasonably withheld", which satisfies the remaining two fallback elements, so we have targeted the fallback and made the single smallest addition: a mutual successor carve-out exercisable on written notice, leaving the consent requirement for all other assignments untouched. No change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists in Section 6, so there is no walk-away trigger.

proposal.summary: Add mutual successor-assignment carve-out on written notice to the nonassignability clause
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a mutual carve-out allowing either party to assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets on written notice, leaving the existing consent standard (not to be unreasonably withheld) intact for all other assignments. This is our fallback position on assignment.
